name: Grammar words
pairs: A person, place, thing or idea.
Noun
An action word, like run or think.
Verb
A word that describes a noun, like blue or tall.
Adjective
A word that describes a verb, often ending in -ly.
Adverb
A word that takes the place of a noun, like she or they.
Pronoun
A word that shows where or when, like under or after.
Preposition
A word that joins words or sentences, like and or but.
Conjunction
A word that shows strong feeling, like wow or oops.
Interjection
The words a, an and the.
Article
Who or what a sentence is about.
Subject
The part of a sentence that tells what the subject does.
Predicate
A word meaning more than one, like cats or children.
Plural
A word that means the same as another, like big and large.
Synonym
A word that means the opposite of another, like hot and cold.
Antonym
Words that sound the same but mean different things, like to, too and two.
Homophone
Letters added to the start of a word, like un- or re-.
Prefix
Letters added to the end of a word, like -ful or -ing.
Suffix
Two words joined to make one, like sunflower.
Compound word
Two words shortened into one with an apostrophe, like can't.
Contraction
A group of words that expresses a complete thought.
Sentence
A group of sentences about one main idea.
Paragraph
The letters a, e, i, o and u.
Vowel
Any letter that is not a vowel.
Consonant
A part of a word with one vowel sound.
Syllable
The main part of a word, before prefixes or suffixes.
Root word
The mark used to end a question.
Question mark
The mark that shows a pause in a sentence.
Comma
Words that start with the same sound, like big brown bear.
Alliteration
